themes.title: How words are counted
mainQuestions: Look at the loop in countWords. Explain how it arrives at the number of words for the string a.
Look at the starting value of words in countWords. Explain why it is not 0.
criteria: Student explains that the function counts the spaces and adds one, so the string a with three spaces gives 4
Student explains that words starts at 1 because a sentence of n words has n minus 1 separating spaces

themes.title: Input the function mishandles
mainQuestions: Look at the calls to countWords with b and c in main. What does each call return, and is that the correct word count?
Suppose the text passed to countWords starts with a space. What would the function return, and why?
criteria: Student predicts 3 for b and 1 for c, recognises that both are wrong (the correct counts are 2 and 0), or admits the function does not handle repeated spaces or empty input
Student explains that every space is counted wherever it appears, so a leading or trailing space adds an extra word

themes.title: Helper functions
mainQuestions: Look at isLetter and countLetters. Explain how countLetters decides which characters to count.
criteria: Student explains that isLetter checks the ASCII ranges for lowercase and uppercase letters and that countLetters adds one for each such character, ignoring spaces
